texts.preamble: Dr. Sk. Asadul Haque vs Food Safety And Standard Authority Of ... on 9 December, 2021 Author: Arindam Mukherjee Bench: Arindam Mukherjee 43 09.12.2021 Ct. No.23 (Nb) In The High Court At Calcutta Constitutional Writ Jurisdiction Appellate Side The petitioner says that a circular was issued by the Food Safety and Standard Authority of India ("in short Fssai")
texts.facts: The petitioner says that a circular was issued by the Food Safety and Standard Authority of India ("in short Fssai") for filling up of the vacancies in the posts of Management Services and Scientific Services in FSSAI on deputation including short term contract/contract (outsource). The petitioner submitted his candidature. Admittedly, the selection process was conducted by FSSAI. A list of suitable candidates were short listed by the Selection Committee and were respectively placed in a recommendation list as serial nos.1 to 9 for being appointed Dr. Sk. Asadul Haque vs Food Safety And Standard Authority Of ... on 9 December, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173024381/ 1 against the vacancy of four technical officers. The recommendation was approved by FSSAI by a memo dated 21 st May, 2012 in the same order as in the recommendation list. The Assistant Director (E&A) of FSSAI forwarded a list of nine candidates respectively placed in serial nos.1 to 9 to the agency 2 engaged for outsourcing technical officers being the respondent no.8. In the memo dated 21st May, 2012 (appearing at page 42 of the writ petition) there is, however, no mentioning of four vacancies in the posts of technical officers. It only says that FSSAI have decided to outsource the services of the following persons in serial nos.1 to 9 through their agencies to give services in FSSAI on consolidated wages for a period upto 31 st July, 2012. The petitioner says that he was never engaged by the agency for rendering services to FSSAI as per the memo dated 21st May, 2012 though his name appeared in serial no.2. On the contrary, the petitioner says that the respondent no.7 who was placed as number 3 in the serial was allowed to join on 11 th June, 2012. The petitioner says that he being placed in serial no.2 ought to have been allowed to join and render services before respondent no.7 who was no.3 in the list. Having not done so, the outsourcing agency as well as FSSAI have acted arbitrarily and in an illegal manner, FSSAI being a government organisation, according to the petitioner could not have resorted to such untransparent arbitral procedure when they themselves had conducted an interview to select suitable candidates and had placed the petitioner in serial no.2 ahead of the respondent no.7 being placed in serial no.3. The petitioner further submits there still lies vacancy in the post of technical officers in FSSAI as per the documents available with the petitioner, though not on record. The petitioner, therefor, should be permitted to join as technical officer, FSSAI. FSSAI in reply submits that they have outsourced the recruitment and had only assisted in preparing a list by conducting a selection process. It is the agency which has given the appointment to respondent no.7. The subject list was prepared in the year, 2012. Last affidavit-in-reply filed by the petitioner was affirmed on 29 th July, 2016 i.e. more than five years prior to this date.
